name: Banking & Finance
description: Banking awareness for IBPS, SBI, RBI and other bank exams.

questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India began operations on 1 April 1935 on the recommendation of which commission?
questions.explanation: The RBI Act, 1934 followed the Hilton Young Commission's recommendations; the RBI was nationalised in 1949.

questions.question: CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio) refers to what?
options: The share of deposits banks must keep as cash with the RBI
The rate at which RBI lends to banks
The interest banks pay on savings
questions.explanation: CRR is the fraction of net demand and time liabilities that banks must park with the RBI as cash — a liquidity tool.

questions.question: The repo rate is the rate at which…
options: The RBI lends short-term funds to banks against securities
Banks lend to each other overnight
questions.explanation: In a repo, banks borrow from the RBI against government securities; the reverse repo is the opposite direction.

questions.question: Who decides the RBI's monetary policy stance and policy rates?
questions.explanation: The six-member MPC (three RBI + three government nominees) sets the policy repo rate to meet the inflation target.

questions.question: The ₹1 note is the only note not issued by the RBI. Who signs it?
questions.explanation: The ₹1 note is issued by the Government of India (Ministry of Finance) and bears the Finance Secretary's signature.

questions.question: Which is India's oldest bank, founded in 1806 as the Bank of Calcutta?
questions.explanation: The Bank of Calcutta (1806) became the Bank of Bengal and eventually the State Bank of India (1955).

questions.question: NABARD, established in 1982, is the apex institution for what?
questions.explanation: NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) refinances banks for farm credit and supervises cooperative banks.

questions.question: SEBI, the regulator of India's securities markets, was given statutory powers in which year?
questions.explanation: SEBI was set up in 1988 as a non-statutory body and given statutory powers by the SEBI Act, 1992.

questions.question: Which body regulates the insurance sector in India?
questions.explanation: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (est. 1999) regulates insurance; PFRDA oversees pensions.

questions.question: The UPI payment system was developed by which organisation?
questions.explanation: The National Payments Corporation of India (est. 2008) developed UPI (launched 2016), RuPay, IMPS and Bharat BillPay.

questions.question: In which year was UPI launched in India?
questions.explanation: UPI was launched in April 2016; it now processes well over 15 billion transactions a month.

questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (financial inclusion) was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: PMJDY (August 2014) opened crores of zero-balance accounts with RuPay cards and overdraft facilities.

questions.question: KYC stands for what?
questions.explanation: Know Your Customer norms require banks to verify customers' identity and address to prevent fraud and money laundering.

questions.question: The Basel norms on bank capital adequacy are issued by which body?
questions.explanation: The BCBS, hosted by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), sets global capital and liquidity standards (Basel I–III).

questions.question: What is the minimum amount for an RTGS transaction?
questions.explanation: RTGS is meant for high-value transfers of ₹2 lakh and above; NEFT has no minimum and settles in half-hourly batches.

questions.question: Banks must lend what share of their Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) to priority sectors (agriculture, MSMEs, etc.)?
questions.explanation: Domestic banks must lend 40% of ANBC to priority sectors; foreign banks have a 32% target (40% with adjusted net bank credit norms).

questions.question: DICGC insures bank deposits up to what amount per depositor per bank?
questions.explanation: Since 2020, the DICGC (a wholly-owned RBI subsidiary) insures deposits up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank.

questions.question: NABARD was set up on the recommendation of which committee?
questions.explanation: The B. Sivaraman Committee (1979) recommended NABARD, which began working in 1982 with ₹100 crore capital.

questions.question: India's Central Bank Digital Currency (e₹) retail pilot was launched by the RBI in which month/year?
questions.explanation: The digital rupee retail pilot began on 1 December 2022 in four cities, after the wholesale pilot on 1 November 2022.

questions.question: MSF (Marginal Standing Facility) is what?
options: An emergency overnight borrowing window for banks at a penal rate
questions.explanation: Under MSF, banks can borrow overnight against SLR securities up to a limit, at a rate above the repo rate — a liquidity backstop.
